clue.text: Snooped round barrel central to exclusive function

indicators.note: round means placed all about, so one word encloses the next

parts.note: to snoop is to pry, so snooped is pried
a vat is a large barrel or tub
central things are inner ones

explanation.surface: Someone nosed around a cask at the heart of a select party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central' looks like part of the surface's location, but it is a separate charade piece meaning inner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner held for invited guests only is a social occasion closed to outsiders, hence exclusive.

clue.text: Player/broadcaster in love with endless Mardi Gras

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the festival's name is dropped
in tells us the zero for love sits inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: MARDI GRA, the carnival name without its last letter, rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A musician or DJ is smitten with a carnival that never quite ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram has no separate signal; the definition's slash lets 'broadcaster' hint at scattering the letters. A radiogram was a cabinet combining radio and record player.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiogram is a piece of furniture combining a gramophone record player with a radio receiver.

clue.text: Man (Latin-American) is source of disease

parts.note: vir is the Latin word for man
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A Latin-American man turns out to be where an illness started.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as 'a Latin-American man' but splits into Latin for man followed by American.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is an infectious microscopic agent that causes many diseases.

clue.text: Far from dominant mixer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a musical scale the keynote, as opposed to the dominant fifth note
second meaning: the fizzy water added to gin and other spirits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from dominant' reads as meek, but in music the dominant is the fifth note of a key and the keynote has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic is the musical name for a key's first note and also the quinine soda used to dilute spirits.

clue.text: Break up book with gloomy oriental covering

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps around and encloses the book abbreviation

parts.note: dismal means gloomy or dreary
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
E for eastern, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: Tear apart a volume wrapped in a gloomy Eastern cover.
explanation.walkthrough: DISMAL covers NT to give DISMANTL, then E for oriental completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it apart piece by piece, the transitive sense of break up.

clue.text: Wandering into Chile in bygone age

indicators.note: wandering things stray from their path, so these letters drift out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller roams into Chile in some long-past era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic is the New Stone Age, the prehistoric period when farming began.

clue.text: Lady Heath

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woman's first name
second meaning: the botanical genus of heathers and heaths

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a titled woman named Heath, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name and also the Latin genus name for heath plants.

clue.text: Fire from Tory Standard — put on a percentage

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a standard is a banner or flag
a ration is a fixed share or portion

explanation.surface: A political row about a Tory flag being adorned with a statistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' just places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a huge blaze that destroys buildings or land.

clue.text: Correct mistake, one in narrow stretch of water

indicators.note: in shows the first three pieces sit inside the word for narrow

parts.note: mean can describe a narrow, petty mind
to edit is to correct text
to err is to make a mistake
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Fix an error where a ship sits in a narrow strait.
explanation.walkthrough: Narrow gives MEAN in its sense of petty or small-minded; the three earlier pieces sit inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean is a sea, a large body of salt water between Europe and Africa.

clue.text: Street cry on Mars?

parts.note: surface reading: a shout heard in the road
setter's reading: the call of the rag-and-bone man, with Mars the alchemists' planet of iron and an ancient god

explanation.walkthrough: Rag-and-bone men, who collected scrap from British streets by horse and cart, called 'Any old iron!'; alchemy linked the planet Mars with that metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrap dealer's traditional call names worn-out metal, and the red planet's alchemical metal fits the question mark.

clue.text: Slags render one coarse

indicators.note: to render is to melt down and reshape, so these letters are recast

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Smelting waste makes one rough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slags is a noun here, the waste from smelting, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoriae is the plural of scoria, the clinker or dross left after smelting metal or from volcanic lava.

clue.text: Mill-bearing strands?

parts.note: setter's reading: the river with a mill on it in George Eliot's novel
surface reading: threads, as from a spinning mill

explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot's novel is The Mill on the Floss, so the river bears a mill; the same word means fine silky threads.
explanation.definitionFit: Floss means soft silk fibres or thread, and is also the river in Eliot's title.

clue.text: Vicar with hairstyle that's burlesque

indicators.note: to style something is to arrange it, so these letters are restyled

parts.note: taken as written
the first part of the word, taken as written; the rest signals the shuffle

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a comically over-the-top haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairstyle' must be split: the first part is fodder and 'style' tells us to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade, a parody performance, so it is a kind of burlesque.

clue.text: Sailor on edge, unable to take any more

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A seaman on the brink, at the end of his tether.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrim means full to the top, a vessel filled so it can hold nothing further.

clue.text: Very small students with copper in the distance

indicators.note: in places the first pair of pieces inside the word for distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Tiny students carrying copper coins far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Students is Britain's student body. The spelling with an I in the middle is a common error; the wordplay confirms the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule means extremely small or tiny, a plain synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Possibly infectious message passed round at church

indicators.note: passed round means wrapped about the following words like a band

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A note that might spread disease is handed around in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A cable is an old word for a telegram, the message sent by wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something catchable, such as a cold, can be caught, so it may well be infectious.

clue.text: One with dire forebodings about oaf and artist

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
an ass is a fool or oaf
taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A doom-monger worried about a lout and a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra, the Trojan prophetess cursed never to be believed, names anyone who predicts disaster.

clue.text: Nefarious ritual made Banquo's head want substance

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter

parts.note: the ghost from Macbeth supplies his initial
to want is to lack
mass is the amount of matter or substance

explanation.surface: A wicked rite made the murdered thane's head crave something solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A black mass is a blasphemous parody of the Christian Mass, a ritual of devil worship.

clue.text: Look back on skirt received by Ceres, perhaps

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so the garment goes inside the goddess's letters
perhaps hints the name is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Ceres, goddess of harvests, is given a short skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ceres is the Roman goddess of agriculture; her letters are shuffled and MINI is placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past times fondly, idiomatically to look back on them.

clue.text: Many a musical moderator

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: Plenty of show-tune lovers act as presenters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is the person presiding over a meeting, who keeps the discussion in order.

clue.text: Co-ownership of paper jumper

parts.note: The Times is a London newspaper
a hare is a leaping animal

explanation.surface: Shared ownership of a newspaper's knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a jumper is a sweater, but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is a holiday property jointly owned, each buyer holding rights to particular weeks.

clue.text: Animal of low bearing

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle
south-east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A creature that carries itself humbly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low bearing' suggests humble posture; low is the cow's call and bearing a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large deer of North America, a wild animal.

clue.text: Garden nuisance inducing boredom

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A pest in the garden that makes the gardener weary.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate signal; the answer simply sits inside the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a French loanword for boredom.

clue.text: Compare with boy holding thousand back

indicators.note: back means the name is read from its end
holding means the name keeps the abbreviation for a thousand inside it

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name
K is short for a thousand, from kilo

explanation.surface: Measure yourself against a lad who is keeping back a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them, pointing out a resemblance.

clue.text: Actress learning name

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A performer memorising someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophia Loren is the Italian film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is a famous Italian film actress, so the clue defines by example.

clue.text: Get round to being pompous

indicators.note: get is taken as produce or make, so these letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Finally do something, being self-important about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get round to' reads as a phrasal verb meaning finally do; the surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes speech that is pompous and inflated, as well as full and resonant.

clue.text: Trump nets king; North leads: it's an ideal situation

parts.note: N is short for north

indicators.note: to net is to catch and enclose, so the king sits inside the name

parts.note: Ivana Trump, first wife of Donald Trump
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A bridge hand: a trump captures the king, North is on lead, and all is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is bridge, but Trump is the surname of Ivana; R goes in after her I, and N goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect bliss, used loosely for any idyllic state.

clue.text: Venice's leaders take up heresy of shunning the flesh

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letters of the city are used

parts.note: the first two letters of the city's name
to take up is to get or acquire
Arianism is the early Christian heresy that denied Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: The Doges of Venice adopt a heretical diet without meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The flesh' here means meat, not the sins of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetarianism is the practice of abstaining from eating meat.
